sections.h2: Where is Caldwell and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Caldwell is the county seat of Canyon County, about 24 miles west of Boise and roughly 17 miles east of the Oregon border. It is part of the Boise metropolitan area and is the fifth most populous city in Idaho.

The town was platted in August 1883 and incorporated on January 15, 1890. The College of Idaho opened in 1891, and Canyon County was established in 1892. The Oregon Short Line Railroad, which became part of Union Pacific, is part of the town's early story. Caldwell counted 59,996 residents in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimated 76,629 on July 1, 2025.

A city that gained that many residents in five years has houses of many ages, and a buyer who needs a loan will care about the age of the roof, wiring and plumbing in each one.

  • Platted 1883, incorporated January 15, 1890
  • Elevation: 2,395 feet
  • City area: about 22 square miles
  • 2020 census population: 59,996
  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 76,629 (Census Bureau)

Caldwell has an agricultural base tied to irrigation canals, with food processing, retail and education layered on top. Wikipedia describes an economy built on agriculture, agricultural processing, commercial retail and the college. Joseph Albertson, who founded the Albertson's grocery chain, is among the town's notable names.

The College of Idaho sits on a 55-acre campus in the city. The city lies about 24 miles from Boise, so a job change anywhere in the Treasure Valley can put a Caldwell household on a moving deadline, and the house then has to sell on that schedule.

Caldwell also has an unusual school setup. Two districts serve the city, Caldwell School District and Vallivue School District, and the Caldwell district is the smallest in Idaho by area at about 22 square miles. A buyer comparing houses will want to know which district a specific address falls into.

sections.h2: What does Caldwell's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Caldwell has a semi-arid climate with hot summers, cold winters and about 11.1 inches of precipitation a year. Daily highs average 93.7 degrees Fahrenheit in August and 38.5 degrees in December, and the mean daily low reaches 22.3 degrees in December.

Records go further than the averages. The recorded high is 112 degrees in August and the recorded low is minus 34 degrees in December. July is the driest month at 0.26 inches and December the wettest at 1.60 inches. Those swings are hard on certain parts of a house:

  • Cooling equipment, which runs through long August highs
  • Roof surfaces and attic ventilation under summer heat
  • Plumbing in crawlspaces and outbuildings during December cold snaps
  • Fences, which the city regulates (see the code section below)

Rain is scarce, so lawns and gardens depend on irrigation water. Ask the county or your irrigation district what your lot's water rights and delivery schedule are, because buyers often want that answer in writing.

sections.h2: What do Caldwell's code compliance rules say about a house you are selling?
sections.html:
Caldwell's Code Compliance Division enforces the city code on rubbish, weeds, vacant buildings, fences, signs and some business uses, and an unresolved violation can slow a sale. The division is part of the Community Development Department.

The city's published rules include several items a seller can check before listing:

  • Owners, renters and managers must keep property free of accumulated or scattered waste material, including personal property exposed to the elements and visible from public view
  • Vacant, open and accessible buildings must be boarded up and secured to prevent unlawful entry
  • Weeds taller than eight inches must be cut down, removed or destroyed
  • Operating a business without a city business license, or from a home without a home occupation permit, is a violation
  • Fence maintenance and sign rules are also enforced

Code Compliance also enforces the zoning code. Some activities need a permit or special approval from the Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing Examiner or the City Council. If you inherited a house that has been vacant, walk the lot, clear the weeds and secure the doors before an inspection, because an open-building violation is easy to avoid.

The Building Safety Division handles permits and inspections, and its inspection request line is (208) 455-4605. If a previous owner built an addition or finished a garage without a permit, a buyer's lender may ask about it. A cash buyer will usually take that risk on, but you should know about it before you sign.

sections.h2: How does Canyon County bill property tax when a Caldwell house sells?
sections.html:
Caldwell is in Canyon County, so the county assessor values the property, the treasurer collects the tax, and the same two annual due dates apply to everyone. The Canyon County Assessor says assessment notices for real property on the regular roll go out in June, and the resulting tax is due December 20.

The Treasurer's tax payments page lists the first half due by December 20 and the second half by June 20. When a due date falls on a weekend, the county extends it: first-half payments for 2026 are due December 21, 2026, because the 20th is a Sunday. The Idaho State Tax Commission adds that you may appeal your assessed value to the county Board of Equalization by the fourth Monday in June.

The Canyon County Assessor FAQ also answers a question buyers and sellers ask: if you buy a home after April 15, you can still apply for the homeowner's exemption, but it counts toward the next tax year. The county explains that net taxable value freezes at a point during the year. If you sell in spring, remind your buyer to file for the exemption in time for the following cycle.

sections.h2: Which disclosure rules apply to a Caldwell seller?
sections.html:
Idaho's Property Condition Disclosure Act applies to most residential sales, including in Caldwell. Under section 55-2504 of the Idaho Code, anyone intending to transfer residential real property, including non-owner-occupied rental property, completes the applicable items on the form prescribed in section 55-2508.

Section 55-2505 lists transfers that do not need the form. They include transfers by a fiduciary in a decedent's estate or trust, foreclosure transfers, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and a transfer by someone who inherited the house and has not lived in it for the past year.

Exempt does not mean silent. A buyer still has the right to inspect, and a seller who knows about a leaking roof or a failing septic system should think carefully before staying quiet about it. Ask a title company or an Idaho attorney about your situation.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a practical choice in Caldwell?
sections.html:
A cash sale is practical when the seller would rather skip repairs, showings and a long listing period. In Caldwell, that includes houses that need work before a lender would approve a buyer's loan, inherited houses, and rentals that have lost their tenants.

  • You inherited a house that sits empty and want to avoid code compliance letters
  • The house has deferred repairs a loan inspection would flag
  • You are relocating and need a firm closing date
  • You own a rental and no longer want to manage it

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as they are, with no commissions and no closing costs charged to the seller by us. We do not promise a price here, and you may turn any offer down at no cost. Get a second opinion from a real estate agent if you want to compare selling methods.

faqs.q: How many people live in Caldwell, Idaho?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 76,629 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 59,996.

faqs.q: When are Canyon County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due December 20 and the second half June 20. For 2026, the first half is due December 21 because the 20th falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: Can I get the homeowner's exemption if I buy a Caldwell house after April 15?
faqs.a: You can apply, but the exemption counts toward the next tax year. Canyon County says the legislature chose April 15 as the deadline because net taxable value must freeze at a set point.

faqs.q: What code violations should I fix before selling a Caldwell house?
faqs.a: Caldwell enforces rules on rubbish, weeds over eight inches, open or unsecured vacant buildings, fences, signs and unlicensed home businesses. Clearing those before you list avoids delays.

faqs.q: Which school district is a Caldwell house in?
faqs.a: Caldwell is served by the Caldwell School District and the Vallivue School District. Confirm the district for a specific address with the district office.
